docs.title: Answers to the RFC's three questions
docs.text:
1. End date: "run date − 2 days" against PLAN § S6 "to yesterday". The frozen code makes a GDELT day final only after file-day d+1 (extract_gdelt.py:97-98). With "yesterday" the closing file-day would be today's, which is partial at 02:37 UTC. The result is the exact defect of the pinned 10-26 row (finding 1), and the incomplete flag would not show it (122). So "to yesterday", read literally, cannot be "the same procedure as S1" for GDELT without reproducing an undercount. For USGS and markets "yesterday" is technically available. This changes the plan's wording, so it is class B, options below (B-2). Whatever the option, the end date must be in UTC (finding 10). "Nothing is lost" holds for the days left out only if the next month's start covers them (finding 3).

2. USGS overlap criterion: byte-equality of rows or equality of daily counts. The frozen procedure produces both files from one query (extract_usgs.py:43-51). events.csv is not a by-product: it is the H3 input (protocol USGS.angular). A count-only criterion would let revised times and coordinates through. Byte-equality will probably block every month, given an extraction on 2026-10-27 08:43 UTC (finding 4). This changes the overlap criterion, so it is class B, options below (B-3). Under any option, the action on failure must be written before the first run, not chosen by the researcher after seeing the differing rows.

3. Location of extend_s6.py. scripts/, as the RFC proposes. council/PIN.md:8 already provides for "a new file there only through an accepted RFC", D10 covers it, and the file produces study data, which council/scripts/ should not. The condition is finding 11: its hash is recorded with every extension, and it changes only by RFC.

docs.title: Revisions and "nothing is lost" / "rows recoverable later"
docs.text:
Under the RFC a prospective row is extracted once, appended, and never revisited (§ 4). Each source behaves differently:

  • GDELT. Export files do not change once published, but their availability does. A file that is 404 or erroring at extraction time is frozen into the row as "missing", and the day's n is lower. The pinned 10-26 row is the first instance (finding 1), and E6 showed two more (finding 5).
  • USGS. Magnitudes, times and coordinates are revised for weeks. An event can cross 5.5 in either direction after the row is appended, which changes n in daily.csv and the H3 input in events.csv.
  • Markets. A revised close C_d changes y_d and y_{d+1}. Because the frozen code downloads the full history, the next month's run sees the revision. Under byte-equality, that blocks the merge.

So "recoverable later" holds only for rows never extracted. A row already appended is either frozen at its first vintage (if later overlaps do not cover it) or blocks every later merge (if they do, under byte-equality). The protocol has no rule on which vintage S7 reads. This is class B (B-4).

docs.title: Both places of execution
docs.text:
Aspect Research container (addendum, D2 applied) GitHub runner (§ 2) Matters for "same procedure as S1"? Code main = analysis-v1 bytes (pin diff empty) checkout of main, same bytes no, if the wrapper's and the modules' sha256 are recorded (finding 11) Network path egress proxy with its own CA; GDELT http:// → 301 → https; urllib's trust of the CA unknown open internet yes: error rate becomes files_missing (finding 6) Yahoo 429 seen on 2026-11-03 unknown yes for availability; no wrong data (finding 15) Time zone of "run date" not stated UTC yes (finding 10) Persistence of GDELT state ephemeral; work folder unspecified committed to data/s6-extension yes for month 2 (finding 3) Write guard, provenance not stated git status guard, run ids yes for audit (finding 12) Python / libm container's ubuntu-latest y printed to 9 decimals; a 1-ulp math.log difference could flip a last digit on the markets overlap (not checked)

S1 itself ran in a local session (journal/2026-10-27-0830.md:1), so neither place is S1's. "Same procedure" can only mean the same code, parameters and attribution, and the error/404 distinction above is where the place can change a row.

docs.title: Class B options (the PO chooses; the Critic does not)
docs.text:
• B-1 (finding 1): the pinned GDELT row 2026-10-26.
  • (a) Keep it as pinned (PIN as written). The overlap compares 10-21..10-25 only, 10-26 is a declared, counted deviation in the prospective set, and the S1 journal's "S6 will re-extract it" is withdrawn on the record.
  • (b) Allow S6 to replace that single row with the re-extraction. This is a change inside the pin (PIN.md:23, class B), recorded as a post-freeze entry with both values kept.
  • Either way, decide before the first run.
  • B-2 (question 1): end date.
  • (a) Plan wording "to yesterday" kept, all arms. GDELT reproduces the partial-closing defect.
  • (b) Common end = run date − 2 days, UTC (the RFC). The plan's wording is amended.
  • (c) GDELT run date − 2, USGS and markets "yesterday". The arms end on different days.
  • B-3 (question 2 and markets): overlap criterion and the action on failure, declared before the first run.
  • (a) Byte-equality of every overlap row, daily.csv and events.csv (the RFC). Any difference blocks the arm.
  • (b) Equality of daily counts blocks. events.csv differences are reported, not blocking.
  • (c) Byte-equality required only on days older than a declared lag. Younger days are reported.
  • For each: whether a failure means "no merge this month" or "merge the new rows and record the differences".
  • For markets, the same choice over the full-history overlap.
  • B-4 (revisions): which vintage of a prospective row S7 analyses.
  • (a) First extraction, frozen. Later differences are recorded only.
  • (b) A single re-extraction of the whole prospective period at a date fixed now, before UNSEAL-prospective, replacing the appended rows.
  • (c) Each day extracted once at a fixed lag after its date.
  • This must be fixed before 2027-04-27. It touches the S7 gate (night item 8).

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
GO with conditions. Each condition is to be met in a revision of the RFC before the PO accepts it; the Critic verifies the revision.

  1. The PO decides B-1 before any run, and the RFC's overlap and cross-check follow that decision (finding 1).
  2. The wrapper specification states that sys.argv is replaced before the GDELT main() and that OUT folders are created (findings 2, 8).
  3. The RFC specifies month k: a per-month work folder, the start rule per arm, a cut-off at s6_cursor.last_extension, and the treatment of rows appended in earlier months (finding 3).
  4. The overlap criterion and the action on failure are the PO's B-3 choice, written in the RFC before the first run, with no case left to a post-hoc researcher decision (finding 4).
  5. The completeness check reports errors separately from 404s per file-day, for both places of execution (finding 6).
  6. The extension manifests record the real window, the wrapper's and the frozen modules' sha256, and the place of execution with its run or session identifier (findings 7, 11, 12).

Recommended answer for D12: yes to the method, but not to the RFC as written: accept a revision that meets conditions 1–6, after the PO has chosen B-1, B-2 and B-3 (B-4 before 2027-04-27), and only after the Critic has verified that revision.

docs.title: What I could not check
docs.text:
• Network behaviour. Whether Python's urllib in the container trusts the egress proxy's CA, how often the tunnel fails, whether the http → https redirect is followed through the proxy as curl saw it, and whether Yahoo answers the frozen extractor (or the runner's address) with 200. No network access was allowed.
  • Revision magnitude. How many USGS rows of 2026-10-01..26 or markets closes have changed since 2026-10-27. Measuring that needs a download.
  • Size of the 10-26 GDELT undercount. Measuring it needs the files and would read y of a prospective day.
  • Byte-for-byte equivalence across Python and glibc versions for math.log and float formatting on 24,821 rows. That needs a run.
  • The Actions quota and the cost line (RFC:96-99). This is the PO's account.
  • The dry run of RFC:106-107. Forbidden today and not the Critic's to perform.
  • The S1 run's own environment (local session, journal/2026-10-27-0830.md): Python version and network path were not recorded.

docs.title: Finding
docs.text:
Severity Where What Rule How to verify minor reports/weekly/2026-W44.md:8 The line reads "Holm-adjusted p:" followed by five values for H1–H5. Rounded to three decimals, those values are equal to results/phase3/holm.json → rows[*].p, the family-level p values that enter Holm. Erratum text (for whoever next edits the report; reports are the weekly routine's output and this note does not edit it):

Line 8, "Holm-adjusted p: H1 …, H5 …": read "p entering Holm (rows[*].p)". The Holm-adjusted p (rows[*].p_holm) are 1 for all five hypotheses. No hypothesis is rejected on the exploration set. (Erratum of 2026-11-04, council/reviews/2026-11-04-w44-erratum.md.)

docs.title: Review 2026-11-06 — the D12 implementation (PR #3) before the first dispatch
docs.text:
Reviewer: Critic (night item 16, council/NIGHT-QUEUE.md row 16). Commit reviewed: 13b9bae (origin/main; PR #3 merged as 43dbc39, which adds 4 files and modifies none: scripts/extend_s6.py, council/scripts/check_extension.py, .github/workflows/s6-extension.yml, council/reviews/evidence/2026-11-06-extend-s6-dryrun.md). Against: council/rfcs/2026-11-01-monthly-extension-runner.md revision 2, §§ R2.1–R2.13; council/FOR-THE-PO.md, Decided, D12 (place = GitHub runner for all three arms; markets: one request a month, any failure ends it, no retry, no change of header, address, place or source; USGS: R2.9 as written), D16 (a), D17 (b), D18 (council text, (ii) = alternative 3), D19 (a, short start).

Method. Read only. sha256sum on the 7 files the dry-run record lists; git diff analysis-v1 -- scripts/extract_gdelt.py scripts/extract_usgs.py scripts/extract_markets.py study/protocol-v0.4.json (the tag was already present locally, no fetch needed); git diff --name-status 43dbc39^1 43dbc39; the workflow parsed with ruby's YAML (PyYAML is not installed here). docs.title: Findings
docs.text: # severity where what rule how to verify 1 major scripts/extend_s6.py:157, 185; .github/workflows/s6-extension.yml:24-25 (matrix gdelt, usgs, markets, max-parallel: 1), :13 (minutes default), :21 (timeout-minutes) run_date is taken per wrapper invocation, and the workflow runs the three arms one after the other with GDELT first and a budget of hours. A dispatch late enough in the UTC day that the GDELT job runs past 00:00 UTC gives USGS and markets a run date one day later than GDELT's, so their end is one day later: in that month the arms end on different days, which is the property of D17 alternative (c), not of the (b) the PO chose. No data consequence (each arm's end is in its manifest, check N uses the arm's own end, the next month covers the gap), but an undeclared departure in effect from "for all three arms". R2.1 step 3 ("take run_date once") is per invocation, so the RFC text does not contradict the code; D17 (b) and R2.2 read as one end per month. D17 (b); RFC R2.2 ("one common end"), R2.10 D17 The three MANIFEST-s6.json of a month carry the same run_date_utc and window[1]. For the first dispatch: a dispatch early in the UTC day, so that the GDELT job ends before midnight UTC 2 major .github/workflows/s6-extension.yml:37-38 if git fetch origin data/s6-extension; then … else git checkout -B data/s6-extension origin/main; fi treats a failed fetch as an absent branch. If the fetch fails for any transient reason on a later dispatch, the branch is re-created from origin/main without s6-work/, the wrapper finds no manifest, and a second markets (or USGS) request is sent in the same month; the later push is then rejected (non-fast-forward, conflicting manifest), so the second attempt also leaves no record on the branch. The RFC's draft (R2.11) has the same construct, so this is not a departure; it is the one path by which the PO's "one request a month" does not hold. It cannot bite on the first dispatch (the branch does not exist yet, so creation from origin/main is the right branch of the if). D12 (iii); RFC R2.9 ("the wrapper's own record blocks a second markets or USGS attempt … even if the workflow is dispatched again") The job log of every dispatch after the first shows the fetch succeeding; the branch never holds two MANIFEST-s6.json for one arm and month. Fix is the Engineer's (distinguish "no such ref" from a failed fetch, and stop on failure) 3 minor council/scripts/check_extension.py:136-139, ALLOWED at :31-41 R2.3's sentence "The check file records whether the two agree" (the cut read from data/events/<arm>/daily.csv versus STATE.json → s6_cursor.last_extension) is not implemented: no key for it, nothing reads program/STATE.json. R2.5's closed list of what the output holds (dates, equal/different, file counts, exception class and status, sha256, run and session ids, pass/fail) does not include event ids; the checker's own docstring adds "USGS event ids". A list of ids for one date is a lower bound on that day's n, and every compared USGS date (2026-10-01 to the cut) is a prospective day (engine/src/mundane/analyze.ts:40, 75). RFC R2.2, R2.4; D18-i From month 2: compare started_at and the last chunk's ended_at in data/events/gdelt/MANIFEST-s6-<month>.json with the threshold 6 minor scripts/extend_s6.py:153-154, 194-201; council/scripts/check_extension.py:138 sha256.checker in MANIFEST-s6.json is taken when the month is opened and reused by later GDELT chunks; the CHECK file copies it. The record is MANIFEST-s6.json (outcome, exception) and CHECK-<arm>.json, not the job colour; the PO and the researcher read those. RFC R2.5, R2.7 After the run: outcome in the three manifests on data/s6-extension 9 note scripts/extend_s6.py:214; .github/workflows/s6-extension.yml:51 The markets and USGS manifest is written before the request (the right order), but it reaches the branch only at the push. A job cancelled or timed out between the two loses the record, and the next dispatch would send a request (the same outcome as finding 2 by another path). cancel-in-progress: false, the seconds those arms take, and the push retries make it unlikely. D12 (iii); RFC R2.9 A cancelled or failed job in the Actions log for a month whose branch has no manifest for that arm 10 note scripts/extend_s6.py:35, 134-139 --place accepts runner only, where R2.1's usage line lists runner|container|local; the wrapper also refuses unless GITHUB_ACTIONS=true. Both follow D12 (iv) and are stated in the wrapper's docstring (:12) rather than in the workflow header. Sound. D12 (iv); RFC R2.1, R2.8 Dry-run record, case "Place other than the runner" (exit 2, no request) 11 note scripts/extend_s6.py:76, 153, 221 The frozen module file is read three times (hash test, manifest hash, exec_module), where R2.1 step 2 says "hashed once and loaded once". On the runner nothing else writes between the reads; no practical gap, but the text and the code differ. RFC R2.1 step 2 Read the three lines 12 note council/scripts/check_extension.py:54, 214 order_ok tests that the dates of run_daily are sorted, but lines_by_date keys rows by date, so a duplicated date row would be collapsed and "strictly increasing" (check N) could not see it. The frozen writers cannot produce one (extract_usgs.py:46-49, extract_markets.py:33-45, extract_gdelt.py:118-124), so no consequence today. RFC R2.5 N Read the two lines 13 note scripts/extract_usgs.py:26-29; D12 USGS rule The USGS attempt is one main() call. From the first month of 2027 the frozen yearly split makes that one call two HTTP requests (start stays 2026-10-01 under D19 (a)). Consistent with "one attempt a month" read as one call, which is how R2.9 and the wrapper define it; the record should keep saying "attempt". D12; RFC R2.9 Read the loop 14 note council/scripts/check_extension.py:103-111 From month 2 the file-day sha256 reference for compared days comes from earlier months' s6-work/*/gdelt/progress.json on the data branch, so the branch must keep every month's folder; nothing prunes it, and nothing says so. RFC R2.4 (R:13) The branch's history each month 15 note council/reviews/evidence/2026-11-06-extend-s6-dryrun.md:3 The dry run was the Chair's session's, which also wrote the code; R2.13 names "the Engineer" and R:14 "the author's". The author ran it, which is what R:14 asks. The record says so itself. RFC R2.13; R:14 Line 3 of the record

docs.title: The two declared departures (workflow header, lines 6-7)
docs.text:
• oracle added to the paths copied from origin/main (:39) and to the paths unstaged before the commit (:49): sound. The RFC's own guard list (R2.1 step 1) already names oracle, and both the wrapper (extend_s6.py:33) and the checker (check_extension.py:29) guard it; the RFC's draft checkout line (R2.11) omitted it, so once the data branch is older than main in oracle/ the guard would refuse every month. oracle is a tracked tree on origin/main (26 files, no .gitmodules), so the git checkout pathspec resolves and the step cannot fail on it.
  • A checker failure does not stop the commit (:47): sound, and needed. The checker exits non-zero only when it could not write (:131-132, :253-258) or crashes; the draft would then have committed nothing, and the month's MANIFEST-s6.json would never reach the branch, so the refusal of a second markets or USGS request (extend_s6.py:106-113, 176-181, which reads that manifest) would not hold on the next dispatch. With the departure, s6-work/ is committed whatever the checker did, and a missing CHECK file is visible as a warning and, to the researcher, as the absence of the file R2.12 step 1 requires before any merge. R2.5's line for check G ("nothing is committed … but the report") is not what the draft did either; the implemented behaviour is the one consistent with R2.9.

No third departure from the RFC text was found beyond findings 1 (in effect), 3, 4 and 10 above.

docs.title: Checked and found in order
docs.text:
• Window arithmetic (D17 b, D19 a, D16 a). run_date from datetime.now(timezone.utc).date() (extend_s6.py:157), independent of TZ (set to UTC anyway, workflow :17); end = run_date − END_LAG for every arm (:38, :185); cut is the date of the last row of data/events/<arm>/daily.csv on main, read as a date only (:81-83), which is 2026-10-26 for the three arms at this commit; GDELT start = cut − GDELT_BACK (:37, :186), 2026-10-20 for month 1, file-days through end + 1 by the frozen code (extract_gdelt.py:97-98); USGS from 2026-10-01 (:36); markets from the frozen start (:230-231). New rows are the dates in (cut, end] (:121). The checker compares GDELT cut − 5 .. cut − 1 (check_extension.py:151-152), adds the cut only when gdelt_cut_compared is true, which in month 1 it is not (no MANIFEST-s6-*.json on main), so 2026-10-26 is neither compared nor counted as new (D16 a). An open GDELT month takes cut, start, end and run_date from RUN.json (:173-174), so a resumed chunk keeps the month's window. "Nothing to do" when end <= cut returns before any folder is created (:187-189). The file-day counts in the dry-run record are consistent with its window.
  • Stop rules (D12 iii; R2.9). Markets: one urlopen with the frozen URL and header (extract_markets.py:21-22, 28-29), one main() call (extend_s6.py:237), any exception recorded and never retried (:238-239), outcome ended-by-stop-rule, exit 5 (:257); a response without chart.result raises inside the frozen code and takes the same path. USGS: the same path. A second dispatch in the same month: the manifest written before the request (:214) closes the folder for those arms (:106-109), and the wrapper exits 5 before loading the module and before any request (:176-181). GDELT: only the frozen four attempts per file (extract_gdelt.py:52-66); exit 1 or 3 resumes next chunk (:250-255). Dry-run cases (3), (4), (4b), (5d) show these paths with no request sent.
  • Guard. Against origin/main, both tests (extend_s6.py:58-68), run before the frozen-bytes test and before any write or request (:141-152) and again after the call (:261-265); the checker repeats it (check_extension.py:57-61). The frozen bytes of the extractor and of study/protocol-v0.4.json are tested against the analysis-v1 blob (:71-78, :146-152). Workflow: git add s6-work/ then git reset -q scripts study data engine oracle council (:48-49), so the main copies staged by the checkout at :39 never enter the commit; s6-work/ is not ignored (.gitignore has no such entry); __pycache__/ is ignored (.gitignore:4), hence sys.dont_write_bytecode = True at :217 before the load at :219-221; the checker imports the standard library only.
  • What is written, and where. The wrapper writes s6-work/<month>/<arm>/{MANIFEST-s6.json, RUN.json} and renames the frozen MANIFEST.json to MANIFEST.frozen.json (:193-214, :241-243); the frozen code writes daily.csv, events.csv, progress.json, MANIFEST.json into the overridden OUT/PROG only (:224, :227, :230; extract_gdelt.py:33-34, 81, 94, 133, 141; extract_usgs.py:44, 51, 58; extract_markets.py:46, 53); the checker writes s6-work/<month>/CHECK-<arm>.json (:259). The workflow commits s6-work/ to data/s6-extension and pushes HEAD:data/s6-extension (:50-51); nothing targets main, results/, data/ or scripts/. The dry-run record's git status and written-paths lists agree with this.
  • Readers untouched. PR #3 modifies no file. The readers of daily.csv/events.csv (engine/src/mundane/h3.ts:38, scripts/phase2a_generator.py:46-48, scripts/phase2a_marginals.py:208-210, scripts/check_gdelt_goldstein.py:35) are unchanged.
  • Sealed sets. Neither script reads data/split/ or study/UNSEAL-* (grep). Rows of data/events/ on main are read for byte comparison per date, with outputs of dates, counts of dates and equal/different (R2.4, R2.5 allow this: GDELT five days, USGS 2026-10-01 to the cut, markets every pinned row). Values copied out of a row: the GDELT incomplete flag (check_extension.py:233, allowed by R2.6), file-day counts, and the USGS ids of finding 4. Check C for markets compares the cut day's close and writes equal/different only (:203-206). The check file's keys come from a fixed list (:31-41, :114-122) and its text is tested against the same pattern as scripts/check-contract.sh:6 (:30, :256-258): identical regex.
  • Pin. git diff --stat analysis-v1 HEAD -- engine scripts data/split data/events study oracle lists only scripts/extend_s6.py (added under D12) and study/UNSEAL-validation (outside the pin, council/PIN.md:3-10). The three extractors and the protocol JSON are byte-identical to analysis-v1 (git diff empty).
  • Checker against R2.5. P (byte prefix of daily.csv and usgs/events.csv, byte-identical MANIFEST.json for the three arms and gdelt/progress.json, :64-77); O per arm with the GDELT file-day sha256 for the compared day and the next (:156-166); C for USGS and markets (:194-206); N (:210-224: after the cut, none after end, every calendar day for GDELT and USGS, no weekend row and the weekdays without a row listed for markets); E for GDELT reporting only (:226-239), with the count of file-days having errors next to S1's; merge rule G, P, N block, O blocks GDELT only (:168-170, :243-246); an outcome other than done runs no check (:247-248).
  • Manifests against R2.7. All listed fields present (extend_s6.py:194-201, :245-259), plus decisions.
  • Dry-run record against R2.13. Cases (1) per arm, (2) twice, (3), (4) with (4b), (5) with (5a)–(5d) are all there with exit codes and "no request" marked; git status before and after; the written paths; the 7 sha256 values all equal to the files at 13b9bae (checked with sha256sum). No number from results/ or from the sealed sets appears in it: its figures are synthetic request counts and counts of dates.
  • Workflow file. Parses (5 steps, 3 arms, 3 inputs); workflow_dispatch only; permissions: contents: write; concurrency without cancel; fetch-depth: 0 so origin/main and the tag are available to the guard and the frozen-bytes test.

docs.title: What I could not check
docs.text:
• The runner itself: that origin/main and refs/tags/analysis-v1 are present after actions/checkout@v4 as assumed, that GITHUB_TOKEN may push to data/s6-extension (branch protection), and the real network from GitHub's hosts. The E6 workflow pushed with the same pattern (program/STATE.json), which is the only evidence.
  • The dry run: I checked its record, not its execution (R2.13). The stub reproduces the fields the frozen code reads, not the services' real payloads (record, "Not checked here").
  • The Actions quota. The RFC ("Cost and risk"; R2.8, "needs from the PO") has the PO confirm it before the first dispatch, spending being class B. No confirmation is on record in council/FOR-THE-PO.md (grep "quota" empty).
  • Night item 13 (the verification of RFC revision 2 against the review's conditions 1–6 and audit decision 2) is still open (council/NIGHT-QUEUE.md row 13: "was not worked; it stays first"). This review is item 16 and does not replace it; the D12 row says its findings reach the PO before the first dispatch, "recommended, not a gate".
  • The behaviour of the workflow when the dispatched ref is not main: the wrapper, the checker and the frozen code are always origin/main's (:39), but the workflow file itself is the dispatched ref's. The first dispatch is the PO's, from main.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Ready for the first dispatch, on these conditions.

  1. The first dispatch (arms: all, the PO's, D12) is made early enough in the UTC day that the GDELT job ends before 00:00 UTC, so that the three manifests carry the same run_date_utc and end (finding 1); the Engineer removes the dependence on the hour of dispatch before the December dispatch.
  2. No second dispatch with arms: all in the same month, and none in a later month, until the Engineer has separated "branch absent" from "fetch failed" at s6-extension.yml:37-38 (finding 2); a GDELT-only continuation (arms: gdelt) is not affected by the stop rule.
  3. The PO's confirmation of the Actions quota is written into council/FOR-THE-PO.md (RFC "Cost and risk"; spending is class B), one line.
  4. After the run and before any merge: the researcher confirms month 1 is merged before month 2 is dispatched (finding 3), and reads the three MANIFEST-s6.json and CHECK-<arm>.json rather than the job status (finding 8).

Findings 3–7 are for the Engineer before the second month; none of them changes a row, a request or the pin. Item 13 remains open and is not a condition of this review.

docs.title: Review 2026 11 06 rfc extension runner rev2
docs.text:
Standing disclaimer

Results on the practice part of the data are never evidence, either way. The validation test (run once, 1 November 2026) and the prospective test (2027) are the only answers; their outcomes appear on this site, in plain words, only after the council's audit and the PO's release.

docs.title: Verification — RFC 2026-11-01 "S6 monthly extension runner", revision 2
docs.text:
Critic, night session 2026-11-06 (night item 13; council 2026-11-03 decision 4, brief extended by council 2026-11-05 decision 7). Scope: council/rfcs/2026-11-01-monthly-extension-runner.md § "Revision 2" (cited RFC:<line>, file at 7d3a8db) against the conditions 1–6 of council/reviews/2026-11-03-rfc-extension-runner.md (cited R:<finding>), audit decision 2 of council/meetings/2026-11-03-audit/decisions.md, and the seven points of the 2026-11-05 brief. Frozen code read at analysis-v1 (git show analysis-v1:scripts/extract_<arm>.py). Nothing was run except git show, git diff, git log, reads and grep. No extractor, no wrapper, no checker, no network. For the record of month 1 I read, on origin/data/s6-extension, the field names and the dates, equal/different values, file counts, sha256 outcomes and run identifiers of s6-work/2026-11/CHECK-gdelt.json and of the three MANIFEST-s6.json. I read no daily.csv, events.csv or progress.json there, no n, close or y of any set, and nothing under results/.

Timing. D12 (council/FOR-THE-PO.md) asked that this verification reach the PO before the first dispatch. It did not: the night of 2026-11-05 did not run (usage limit, D21), and the PO's local session dispatched on 2026-11-06 at 19:50:44 UTC, after the Critic's item 16 (council/reviews/2026-11-06-extension-runner-impl.md). Month 1 is not affected by anything below: its GDELT overlap is 5 of 5 equal, the file-day sha256 outcomes are 6 of 6 equal, and 0 of its 17 GDELT file-days have errors (CHECK-gdelt.json → checks.O, checks.E).

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Verified on conditions 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 and on audit decision 2. Condition 4 is not verified for one case: a GDELT overlap difference from month 2 on blocks every later month, and nothing says so or what follows (finding 1). That case needs the PO's rule before the December dispatch (class B, D22). The two majors of item 16 are also in the RFC text (findings 2–3), and night item 17 already carries them.

Condition Outcome One line 1 (B-1 decided before any run; overlap and cross-check follow it) verified D16 (a) recorded in 05b6994 (2026-11-06 07:45:46 UTC), before the dispatch at 19:50:44 UTC; R2.4 compares 10-21..10-25 (RFC:278); R2.13 corrects the cross-check to five days (RFC:506); month 1's check lists 10-26 as not_compared 2 (sys.argv replaced; OUT folders created) verified R2.1 steps 4 and 7 (RFC:188-189, RFC:199-202) and the illustration (RFC:224-233) match extract_gdelt.py:89-94, extract_usgs.py:44, 51, extract_markets.py:46, 53 3 (month k: folder, start rule, cut-off, rows appended earlier) verified, with two residuals folder s6-work/<YYYY-MM>/<arm>/ (RFC:249-252); start rule under each D19 alternative (RFC:261-266), decided as a-short; the cut is read from the data file on main, not from s6_cursor.last_extension as the condition said, for a stated reason (RFC:253-255). Residuals: the cut does not move after a blocked month (finding 1); the month name is taken per arm invocation (finding 3) 4 (criterion and action on failure declared before the first run, nothing left to a post-hoc decision) not verified for one case D18 was decided before the run (05b6994) and is written into the checker. But a recurring GDELT block is left open (finding 1), and the RFC carries no acceptance record although RFC:173 promises one (finding 4) 5 (errors reported apart from 404s, reporting only) verified R2.6 (RFC:312-323); the merged row stays as written (RFC:317-319); month 1 reports file_days_with_errors 0 of 17 next to S1's 0 of 4,269 6 (real window, sha256 of wrapper and frozen modules, place and run id) verified R2.7 (RFC:325-341); the three month-1 manifests carry window as run, run_date_utc, started_at, sha256, git_head, place with GITHUB_RUN_ID, attempt, workflow ref, Python and platform Audit decision 2 (a) plan/pin start-rule conflict verified put to the PO inside D19 (RFC:258-259, RFC:418-421); answered by D19 (a-short, "a row appended earlier") 2 (b) B-1..B-4 together, before any run verified RFC:381-382; D16–D19 recorded together in 05b6994, before the dispatch 2 (c) condition 5 is reporting only verified RFC:317-319 2 (d) USGS double count across the cut verified check C (RFC:299), D18-ii and D18-iii (RFC:398-408); the residual of an id change is named 2 (e) markets stop rule verified R2.9 (RFC:362-368); accepted as D12 (iii)

docs.title: Findings (ranked)
docs.text:
# Severity Where What Rule How to verify 1 major RFC:253-255 (cut = last row on main), RFC:263 (a-short compares c_k − 5..c_k), RFC:298 (O blocks "as accepted in D18"), RFC:374-375 ("Consequence": markets only); council/FOR-THE-PO.md D18 A GDELT block recurs every month, and no rule says what follows. If month k's GDELT merge is blocked, nothing is appended, so c_{k+1} = c_k. Month k+1 then starts at the same c_k − 6 and compares the same dates against the same stored rows, which D19 (a) never changes. If the difference comes from the stored row (a file-day that has more or other files at the later extraction), it recurs at every later month. The GDELT prospective series then stops at c_k until S7. The RFC states this consequence for markets only (RFC:374-375), and D18 does not state it. Ending such a block later would be a choice made after seeing the difference, and it changes which GDELT rows S7 reads. Month 1 did not block: its compared days are pinned rows, and all five were equal. From December the compared days (2026-10-30..2026-11-04 if month 1 is merged) are month-1 rows. Month 1 had 0 file-days with errors, so the transient-error route is closed for those rows. A 404 at first extraction that is filled later, and the warm-up route (finding 6), remain CHARTER § 4.3 (decide before the run); condition 4; D19 (a) read the cited lines; trace month k+1 after a blocked month k 2 major (known: item 16 major 2; night item 17 (2)) RFC:465-466; claim at RFC:483-484 In the workflow text, a failed git fetch origin data/s6-extension looks the same as an absent branch. The branch is then re-created from main without s6-work/. The wrapper then finds no record of the month and sends a second markets or USGS request. So the claim "the wrapper's own record blocks a second markets or USGS attempt … even if the workflow is dispatched again" (RFC:483-484) is false in that case. The merged workflow has the same lines D12 (iii); R2.9 read the lines; .github/workflows/s6-extension.yml has the same if git fetch … else … origin/main 3 major (known: item 16 major 1; night item 17 (1)) RFC:185 (step 3, run_date "once" per invocation), RFC:249 (month named by "the arm's first invocation"), RFC:441, 451-453 (minutes 300, max-parallel: 1, GDELT first); scripts/extend_s6.py:157, 161 run_date is fixed once per arm invocation, not once per month. GDELT runs first, for up to 300 minutes, so USGS and markets can start on a later UTC date and get a different end. Addition to item 16: the month's name comes from the same per-invocation date (extend_s6.py:161). A dispatch late on the last day of a month can therefore file GDELT under month k and USGS and markets under month k+1. Item 17 (1) should fix the name together with run_date and end R2.2; D17 (b) (one rule for all arms) read the lines 4 minor RFC:3 (status "draft, revision 2 … for the Critic's verification … then the PO"); RFC:173 ("written into its code and into this RFC's acceptance record") The RFC has no acceptance record. D16–D19 were decided before the run, but they are recorded only in council/FOR-THE-PO.md (05b6994), in the wrapper's header (scripts/extend_s6.py:7-12) and in each check file's decisions. Condition 4 asked for them "written in the RFC before the first run". The substance is met; the letter and the RFC's own promise are not condition 4; R:11 grep -n -i acceptance on the RFC: only line 173 5 minor (also item 16 finding 5, on the code) RFC:243-244 (R2.2: "complete when the run starts after 00:15 UTC"); RFC:263 and RFC:278 (R2.3/R2.4: "closed from a complete file-day", undefined); FOR-THE-PO D18 ("complete on the clock"); council/scripts/check_extension.py:92-100 "Complete file-day" has three readings. R2.3 and R2.4 do not define it. R2.2 gives the only clock rule: after 00:15 UTC, a margin for the publication of the 23:45 file. D18 says "on the clock". The checker tests started_at >= cut + 2 days, 00:00 UTC. Under D17 (b) that test is always true, because run_date = cut + 2 and started_at falls on run_date. Item 16 called the effect mostly conservative, because a missing file blocks the merge rather than passing a wrong row. Finding 1 adds that such a block recurs. So a month dispatched between 00:00 and 00:15 UTC would have its cut row compared the next month, although the cut row's last file may not have been published. The result would be a "different", which then recurs (finding 1). The dispatch times so far (19:50 UTC) are far from the edge D18-i; CHARTER § 4.3 read the lines; month 1 started_at 2026-11-06T19:50:51Z 6 note RFC:282-290 (warm-up precision); extract_gdelt.py:108-114, 130 Read and confirmed: seen_j = A_j \ seen_{j−1}. The necessary condition is correct, and it is stricter than the RFC states. By induction the difference set after file-day j is D_j = seen^ref_{START−1} ∩ A_START ∩ … ∩ A_j. Row d is counted from file-days d and d+1 (:116), so it can differ only through an ID in D_{d−1} or D_d with SQLDATE = d. Every such ID is listed in file-day START − 1. If an ID keeps its SQLDATE across files (not checkable without the files), it is an event dated d ≥ START + 1 that appears in an export of the day before START, which would be a future date. "Conservative, not a wrong row" follows for the compared rows: they are never merged, and under D18 a difference blocks. It does not follow from check O for the new rows. The same chain is the only route by which the warm-up could change a merged row, and O cannot see it. That needs an event listed in file-day START − 1 and dated after the cut #17; R:13 read the lines 7 minor RFC:288-290; extract_gdelt.py:59, 62, 66, 129; CHECK-gdelt.json → checks.O.file_day_sha256 (dates 10-21..10-26) The file-day sha256 report does not separate the two causes of a "different" in every case. (i) A different input on file-day START changes seen_START and can make row START + 1 differ while file-days START + 1 and START + 2 read "equal". File-day START (10-20 in month 1) is not in the report. (ii) A 404 and a persistent error both add "" to the file-day digest (:62, :66, :129), so the digest cannot tell them apart; the missing/errors counts can. Under finding 1 this report is what the PO's rule would act on, so its coverage matters R:13; condition 5 read the lines and the six dates in the month-1 check 8 note (also item 16 note 11, on the code) RFC:182-184 ("hashed once and loaded once"), RFC:190-191; scripts/extend_s6.py:217-221; .gitignore:4 spec_from_file_location + exec_module read the file again, and they would execute a valid scripts/__pycache__/*.pyc if one existed. sys.dont_write_bytecode stops writing a .pyc, not reading one. So the bytes executed are not the bytes hashed. On the runner the checkout is fresh and __pycache__/ is git-ignored, so no .pyc exists and the risk is nil at the declared place. The sentence is inexact. The guard's --exclude-standard does not see git-ignored files, as RFC:190-191 says R:11 (the record shows which code wrote which month) read the lines 9 note RFC:398-406 (D18-ii), RFC:489-490 (R2.12 step 2) Exhaustive only if alternative 4 is split in two, and step 2 is stated for one alternative only. Alternative 4 can mean "skip day d" or "stop the month's rows at d − 1". Skipping day d fails check N ("every calendar day present", RFC:300), and under D19 (a) the gap is permanent: the next cut is past d. That contradicts "a gap that may recur". Stopping at d − 1 can recur. Step 2's "byte for byte as the frozen code wrote them" holds only for alternative 3; for 1, 2 and 4 the step is not written. Moot: the PO chose alternative 3 D18-ii; R2.12 read the lines 10 note FOR-THE-PO D18 (ii) ("already in the pinned events.csv") vs check C (RFC:299, "already present in events.csv on main") From month 2 an id can repeat one appended in month 1, which is on main but not pinned. The decided text covers the pinned file only; the check covers main. Under alternative 3 the action is the same (append as written, report), so nothing changes. The decided wording is narrower than the check D18 read both texts 11 note RFC:409-410 (D18-iv) Only one alternative is stated ("append as written … the only alternative that uses frozen-code output unchanged"). The others are not listed: recomputing the first new y from the stored close (a row the frozen code did not write); withholding the first new markets row; blocking the month's markets merge. Moot: the PO decided (iv) "append as written, record equal/different" R2.10 ("every alternative with its consequence") read the lines 12 note brief point 4: "the readers of daily.csv/events.csv are analyze.ts:89, holm.ts:165-166, h3.ts:38" Two of three confirmed. engine/src/mundane/analyze.ts:89-90 is the outcome column of each arm's daily series (n, n, y). h3.ts:38 is the events.csv reader (id,time_utc,lat,lon,…). holm.ts:165-166 reads gdelt.h1[…] and usgs.h1[…], the aggregates from analyze's results (the H4 input), not either file. holm depends on the files only through analyze. The RFC's own citation analyze.ts:75-77 (days from 2026-10-01 are prospective) is correct. No new search was made claims vs code read the lines 13 note (also item 16 note 13) RFC:369-370 (R2.9 USGS); extract_usgs.py:26-29, 44, 51 The USGS stop rule is coherent with R2.8 (no change of place after a refusal) and with D12 (iii) (any failure ends it, no retry). It is presented as the PO's ("The PO may decide otherwise in D12 … new in revision 2"), and D12 accepted it "as written". Precision: from January 2027 one USGS attempt is two HTTP requests (yearly windows, :26-29). A failure of the second discards the first, because nothing is written before the loop ends (:44, :51). "One attempt" means one call of main(), and R2.9 says no more than that D12 (iii); R2.8 read the lines 14 note RFC:268-272, RFC:417 Arithmetic correct. A run on 2026-11-15 under D17 (b): end 11-13, file-days 10-01..11-14 = 31 + 14 = 45, 45 × 96 = 4,320 files. docs.title: Decisions made (before running what depends on them)
docs.text:
• Log-rate transformation: log(n + 0.5) for counts, log(y) with y > 0 for markets. Reason: the simplest one that handles the zeros; it only serves to estimate generator parameters and does not touch any confirmatory estimate (§ 4.5).

Which one to use is up to S2.2; the planned conservative criterion: the most persistent structure (more dependence = wider null).
  • ACF lags by row index: for markets they are trading days, not calendar days (written in the JSON).

docs.title: Problems
docs.text:
• GDELT: the drift is not linear in the log (185 → 147 → 72 → 39 → 34 per year); the linear ramp leaves structure in the residual. The weekly amplitude (0.33) is above the assumed 0.20 and not sinusoidal (ACF at 7 > ACF at 1). S2.2 must reproduce the shape of the drift, not just its amplitude.

docs.title: Decisions made (before running what depends on them)
docs.text:
• Drift and long memory as a slow AR(1), not as the real curve. Copying the real yearly means would have put real y into the generator (forbidden by the plan). The slow component has a random sign/realisation. Reason: § 4.2, the simplest that reproduces the measured ACF (fit rmse ≤ 0.009 on all arms).
  • Weekly as a per-day profile, with a random rotation if the dates are not given. Reason: S2.1 showed that for GDELT it is not sinusoidal.
  • NB k = min(k on the log scale, k on the raw scale). Calibrating on the log residual alone gave USGS k = 6.0 with synthetic raw variance 1.78 against 3.78 real; on the raw scale GDELT is already above the real variance even with Poisson (k = ∞). The smaller k is kept: more dispersion, wider null (§ 4.2, conservative). Implementation detail of the generator: it does not touch any confirmatory estimate.
  • Markets: Gaussian |ε| noise with no free parameters; the 313 days with y = 0 are not reproduced (the generator produces no zeros).
  • The parameter JSON lives in results/phase2a/ and the engine tests read it from there; S2.3 will use drawArm with those parameters, not the frozen COUNTS_MODEL (which stays in the protocol as the value assumed in Phase 0).

docs.title: Problems

docs.title: Decisions made (before running what depends on them)
docs.text:
• Data days = the arm's whole calendar window, not the validation days. Reason: the plan says "Phase 0 … with the measured parameters", and Phase 0 used the whole window. The confirmatory sets are smaller (about 2–3 months in 12), so the real MDE will be larger: this goes in the report as a limitation.
  • Gate read at the primary filter (none), not at the best filter as Phase 0's verdict did. Reason: the primary filter is fixed by v0.4 (HP_WINDOW_PRIMARY = null). This is the more conservative reading. by_class is computed at the primary filter even when calibration disqualifies that filter, so that the number exists.
  • Power also at the H1 per-test level α/8. Under amendment #27, p_H1 = 8·min p, so at Holm's first step a single test needs p ≤ 0.00125, which with 1000 surrogates means p = 1/1001. Phase 0's α = 0.01 overstates the confirmatory power. This is descriptive only, and the gate stays on Phase 0's definition. It does not change any random stream: the α = 0.01 numbers are the same with or without it, as checked on the smoke run.
  • Markets filters: for the robustness variants, the high-pass runs on the calendar grid for the sky and on the rows for y (window in rows). The primary filter (none) only centres both sides, so it is unaffected. The choice is an implementation detail checked by the calibration. Calibration draws y on random trading-day rows (random weekday rotation, as in Phase 0), with the real calendar offsets on the sky side.
  • Wide calibration grid for markets: 1201-01-01 to 2398-12-31, inside the mundane profile, so that a 98-year window ± 340 years fits.

docs.title: Problems
docs.text:
• GDELT, primary filter not calibrated under the measured generator (0.070 at 0.05, KS p 0.017; tolerance 0.066 and 0.02). The rate at 0.01 is within tolerance (0.020 against 0.030). The 180d filter fails too, while 365d and 90d pass. The S2.2 generator is deliberately wider than the real series (synthetic variance +37%, slow AR φ 0.995), so the failure may reflect the generator being more extreme than reality. The rule, though, says a disqualified filter is not used. The plan does not say what happens when the primary filter of a primary arm fails. Switching the GDELT primary to 365d or 90d would change what the confirmatory test estimates, so under Charter § 4.4 it is a post-freeze amendment that I do not make. It is recorded as blocked, with what the PO needs to decide. S3 and the markets runs do not depend on it.
  • GDELT's class 1 (0.0365) and class 2 (0.0469) are above the MEI. This is not a stop condition (the gate is class 0), but the protocol requires declaring it at the opening of the report (PHASE2 § 4).
  • In the result files the protocol stamp reads v0.3: it comes from the engine's transcription of the frozen parameters, which v0.4 did not change for these keys. The step and the v0.4 parameters used are given in the journal.
  • The USGS run went over the session budget. I let it finish rather than lose 58 minutes of computation.

docs.title: Decisions made (written before the tests were run)
docs.text:
• Scope: end to end through runAnalyze, GDELT arm. The unit tests of S3.1 already cover the pieces (RowSky, H2, H3, guard). S3.3 adds tests that call the full runAnalyze with the real sky grid (ephemerides), the real exploration row pattern of the split, and the protocol's shift set (spawn(1), 1000 surrogates). Only y is synthetic. GDELT is used because its grid costs about 2 s; markets (±340-year grid) and the USGS H3 (≈ 13 min per run) are too slow for 50 windows. Markets and USGS are covered by the numeric-contract run below and by their unit tests.
  • Rows. Every calendar day from 2015-02-19 to 2026-09-30 whose month the split assigns to exploration. Only data/split/months.csv is read; no daily series is read.
  • Synthetic y. The measured GDELT generator (results/phase2a/generator.json, drawArm), weekday profile keyed on the rows' real ordinals.
  • Recovery (n = 2, δ = 0.02, ±0.005). The tilt is betaForEffect(c_rows, 0.02) on the aggregate harmonic-2 series at the rows, as in Phase 2a. Two checks: (a) one draw with the generator's noise only (NB around a constant rate, measured mean and k, no structure): |δ̂ − 0.02| ≤ 0.005 and p < 0.05; (b) the full measured structure: the mean δ̂ of 12 independent draws within ±0.005 (a bias check; with the full structure one draw's sd is about the size of the tolerance, per the S2.3 MDE).
  • Calibration under H0 on 50 windows. 50 pseudo-real windows: the exploration row pattern (offsets from 2015-02-19) moved to 50 random calendar starts between 1950-01-01 and 2070-12-31, one independent H0 draw from the full measured generator per window. Criterion, fixed now: for each of the five confirmatory-type tests run on GDELT (H1 aggregate at n = 2, 3, 4, 6 and the H2 trend), at most 7 of 50 p-values ≤ 0.05 (P(X ≥ 8) ≈ 0.003 for Binomial(50, 0.05)); and over the 250 p-values pooled, the share ≤ 0.5 between 0.35 and 0.65 (p not degenerate). Known context: in S2.3 the unfiltered GDELT null gave 0.070 at 0.05 on 400 windows. The test checks the machinery, not that open question; whatever it gives is reported.
  • Determinism. Two runAnalyze calls on the same rows and y give the same JSON, apart from elapsed_s.
  • Numeric contract. pnpm mundane analyze on synthetic files for GDELT (--series) and USGS (--series and --events, 20 invented events): neither stdout nor the written file contains a body, aspect, house or sign name. Added to tests/contract/mundane-numeric-contract.test.ts.
  • S3.4 brought forward in the same session (same phase, inside the budget; Charter § 2). Decisions for holm, written before the code was run:
  • inputs are the three analyze JSONs of one set (gdelt, markets, usgs); holm refuses files from different sets or protocols, or a missing arm;
  • p_H1 = min(1, 8·min p) over the aggregate H1 p of harmonics {2, 3, 4, 6} × {GDELT, markets}; p_H2 = min(1, 2·min p) over the H2 trend p of GDELT and markets; p_H3 = min(1, 8·min p) over the 8 H3 tests; p_H5 = 1. All as amendment #27; Holm step-down at α = 0.05 over m = 5;
  • H4: first Holm runs with p_H4 = 1. If H1 or H3 is rejected, p_H4 is computed and Holm is run again with it (amendment #27: "computed only if H1 or H3 is rejected"). The harmonic is the one of the minimum H1 p over the 8 H1 tests; a tie goes to the lower harmonic (simplest). The statistic is δ̂_GDELT − δ̂_USGS of the aggregate at that harmonic; the null is the same difference under each shift present in both arms' shift lists (same global shift for both arms), upper tail, (1 + #{null ≥ obs}) / (1 + n);
  • to make this possible analyze now also writes, for each H1 aggregate, the shift list and the null δ̂ of each shift (shifts, null_values). This adds output only; no estimate changes.
  • The S2.3 gate for an uncalibrated markets arm is not implemented: markets passed its calibration in S2.3 (0.045 at 0.05, KS p 0.22, results/phase2a/summary.json), so the gate does not apply.

docs.title: Decisions made (before running what depends on them)
docs.text: Written at 17:42 UTC, before any code or run of E4. - STATE.next = S4.1 is still blocked on the PO (GDELT primary filter). As in the four previous sessions I continue S4.2 on arms that do not depend on the block: E4 on markets and USGS, exploration set only. - E4 (Tier 2 surrogates with the Sun pairs), definition. The sources (protocol v0.3 § 3.2 and § 4.1, amendment #2) say only that the Sun pairs "enter only in Tier 2 and are declared secondary", and that Tier 2 is the free global shift of ±[7, 45] days. Choices, conservative and with no new estimator: - Null: tier2Shifts() as already in surrogates.ts, i.e. all 78 candidates ±7..±45 days (fewer than N_SURROGATES = 1000, so no draw), global shift as in Tier 1, same for both arms. docs.title: Decisions made (before running what depends on them)
docs.text:
Written at 07:39 UTC, before any code or run of E5. E5 is exploratory (amendment #25), so none of this changes a confirmatory estimate; the choices follow charter § 4 (literal text first, then most conservative, then simplest).

  • What E5 is. Plan S4.2: "E5 robustness filters 365/180/90 computed within the set, block by block". Source of the filter role: protocol v0.3 § 4.2 (the high-pass filter is a declared robustness check of the primary estimator), HP_WINDOWS_ROBUSTNESS = [365, 180, 90] in study/protocol-v0.4.json. So E5 = the H1 aggregate estimator at the primary harmonics {2, 3, 4, 6}, with the high-pass filter applied to both y and the sky series, one test per harmonic × window: 12 tests per arm. No class split, no H2/H3 under filters (not named by the plan; adding them would widen the closed list).
  • Block. Amendment #24: "the filtered variants are computed within the set, monthly block by block". Read as: a block is a maximal run of consecutive calendar months that all belong to the set; the filter runs on each block separately and never reads across a gap (so never near a row of another set). The other reading (each single month is a block) would make all three windows identical (every window exceeds a month), so it cannot be what a list of three windows means. Exploration blocks are 1–8 months long (USGS era from 1990: 111 blocks; markets from 1928: 308 blocks), so: the 365 window is longer than every block and reduces to removing each block's mean (the oracle's rule window ≥ length → subtract the mean, highpass in statistics.ts); 180 does so on blocks of ≤ 6 months; 90 filters blocks longer than 3 months. This is a consequence of #22 + #24, reported as such, not changed.
  • Filter. The engine's highpass (centred moving average, odd kernel, reflect padding, mean removal when the window ≥ block length), unchanged, applied per block. Window counted in rows: calendar days for USGS (zero days are rows), trading days for markets, as Phase 2a applied hpApply(y, hp) to the markets rows.
  • Sky side. The same block-wise operator F is applied to the sky rows of every shift: for shift s, c_s = c at (row grid index + s), then F(c_s). Estimator as Phase 2a's RowProjection.deltaHat: δ̂_s = Σ F(y)·F(c_s) / (mean(y) · Σ F(c_s)²) · Var(c_0 raw rows). One-sided upper p = (1 + #{δ̂_s ≥ δ̂_0}) / (1 + n).
  • Null. The arm's own shifts as in analyze and E1–E3 (armShifts(arm, new Rng(SEED)), stream path 1): Tier 1 for USGS, the 340-year null for markets. Each arm run once; output results/phase3/exploratory/<arm>-e5.json.
  • No BH-FDR here: it is applied once at the end of S4.2.

docs.title: Decisions made (before running what depends on them)
docs.text: Written at 22:38 UTC, after the data check and before any E6 code or run. - Data. Actions run 41225487118 finished; MANIFEST-goldstein.json on data/gdelt-goldstein says done: true, cursor 2546/2546. Brought daily-goldstein.csv, MANIFEST-goldstein.json, progress-goldstein.json to main (file checkout from the data branch; the branch's older journal/state files are not merged). scripts/check_gdelt_goldstein.py --set exploration: exit 0, 2472/2472 days present, 2 days whose n_pos + n_neg differs from daily.csv (2015-04-02, 2015-05-16), both with a different number of files read, 0 with the same file set. Report in data/events/gdelt/CHECK-goldstein.json. - E6 (GDELT by Goldstein sign), definition. Two strata of the exploration-set GDELT days: pos (n_pos, events passing the primary filter with GoldsteinScale > 0) and neg (n_neg, GoldsteinScale < 0; the filter leaves no zero). Per stratum, with no new estimator, tail or null, exactly as the E7 H1 part: the H1 aggregate (all 14 pairs) at harmonics 2, 3, 4, 6 on the stratum's daily count series (same rows as daily.csv for the set, zero days included, unfiltered as the primary estimator), against the GDELT Tier 1 global-shift null, same seed and stream as H1, one-sided upper p. 8 tests. "By sign" is read as the two strata side by side; no difference test between strata. Reason: the estimator the protocol already uses on this arm, applied to each stratum, as for E7. - The 2 days whose split total differs from daily.csv. Used as extracted (the stratum counts are those of the E6 extraction); the rows are not dropped and not rescaled. Reason: dropping or adjusting days after looking at them would be a choice on the data; the difference is ≤ 13 events on 2 of 2472 days and comes from the file set the server returned, not from the method. The code requires the split's dates to equal the set's rows exactly and writes the number of differing days into the result. Implementation detail, does not change what E6 estimates. - No q-value in this run. BH-FDR once, after every E1–E7 test of all arms is in (E6 is the last one). - BH-FDR across E1–E7, definition. Written at 22:45 UTC, after E6 ran and before any q-value was computed. With E6 in, every test of the closed list is in: 14 files under results/phase3/exploratory/, 311 tests (E1 168, E2 36, E3 15, E4 24, E5 36, E6 8, E7 24). One family of all 311, as decided on 2026-10-29 (journal/2026-10-29-0237.md). Input: each test's raw one-sided p exactly as stored, no test dropped or merged (E2 at n = 2, 3, 4, 6 repeats the H1 aggregate estimator but is a declared part of E2's spectrum, so it stays). Method: the Benjamini–Hochberg step-up procedure (the one the protocol names, STOPPING.exploratory and amendment #25), q_(i) = min over j ≥ i of min(1, m·p_(j)/j), m = 311; ties keep their order of appearance (q does not depend on it). Reported at the threshold q < 0.05 (the one plan step S7 uses for replication). Code: scripts/bh_fdr.py, which reads only the result files (no sky, no y). Output: results/phase3/exploratory/bh-fdr.json, tests identified by file, analysis and index fields only (V3).

• Engineer: two obstacles, independent: (1) network; (2) the frozen extractors take end from the protocol (2026-10-26) and cannot be edited (pin; D10). Path 1: runner RFC on a GitHub runner; needs Critic review (D10), D12 accepted by the PO, the PO adds scripts/extend_s6.py and the workflow and confirms the Actions quota; class B; it addresses both obstacles and does not need D2. Path 2: D2 applied (Custom allowlist, three hosts); class B; fixes obstacle (1) only, recommended first because it costs least. Path 3: the PO or the local helper runs the frozen extractors elsewhere; class B with D10; fallback only. Not paths: a proxy or mirror to defeat the 403; another source; cached or synthetic fill; a wrapper under council/scripts/; editing the extractors' END. Class A today: schedule the Critic's review of the RFC ahead of night item 2; refresh STATE.network.
  • Researcher: block since 2026-11-02, owner engineer (program/STATE.json). Needs: PO applies D2 and decides the RFC (class B, after the Critic's review), or the extension runs outside the cloud. Reading of the RFC, for the Critic to confirm: the runner executes on a GitHub runner and may not need D2 for its own fetch; D12 is needed in any case. Next research session 2026-11-03 at 02:37 UTC (D8), under the same block unless D2 is applied or D12 is decided.
  • Critic (Round 2): Path 3 listed the BigQuery route for GDELT as a class B fallback; classed C, because the frozen GDELT.source is the export files named in study/protocol-v0.4.en.md, and BigQuery is not "same procedure as S1" (program/PLAN.md). Paths 1 and 2 touch no pin. Recommended the review of the RFC ahead of night item 2 (conditions: findings only; no code; no extractor run; answers to the three RFC questions; where an answer changes the plan's wording "yesterday" or the USGS overlap criterion, the choice goes to the PO; item 2 takes the following night). Noted that D12 is already open and that D2 is off the critical path for the runner if D12 is accepted. Noted that program/STATE.json and FOR-THE-PO.md still tie the extension to D2 and should be reworded (class A).
  • Integrity (Round 2): Paths 1 and 2: no breach. Path 3: no breach only if the frozen code is used unchanged. Condition: D12 does not go to the PO without the Critic's review and its answers on the end date, the USGS equality criterion and the location of extend_s6.py. Writes to program/STATE.json: the research loop writes it (charter § 5.3); a council role does not; the STATE.network refresh goes through the research session, and the Engineer records a dated probe that the researcher may copy.

docs.title: Cielo-Eventi — week 2026-W45
docs.text:
Cielo-Eventi tests, with rules fixed in advance, whether the positions of the planets say anything about events on Earth: large earthquakes, big daily moves of the US stock market, and world news events. It is built so that it can fail: "nothing found" is a valid answer.

Where we are: stage 4 of 6, waiting for new data. The program is paused on one decision.

Needs Francesco: choose where the monthly new-data download runs (the council recommends an automated GitHub runner) and what happens if a source refuses it.

This week - The sealed part of the data was opened once, as planned, and tested. - The November download could not start until that decision is made.

What it means - The first real test showed no sign of an effect. It cannot be repeated, and it does not rule anything out: the final test on new data comes after April 2027.

Next - Download the new data once the decision is made.

Technical details: https://github.com/sisco128/cielo-eventi/blob/main/journal/INDEX.md
